description: A predator-prey oscillator: a population of prey and a population of predators chase each other round a cycle about a quarter of a turn apart.

params.text: Sets the speed the simulation runs at, -8 to +4 octaves; the centre gives C4 at 261.63Hz and the bottom about 1Hz.
Sets the asymmetry between the two populations, 0 to 1: in Lotka-Volterra it is the predator-prey timescale ratio and the relative swing, and in Rosenzweig-MacArthur the predator's efficiency.
Sets the size of the boom and bust, 0 to 1: in Lotka-Volterra a target the amplitude servo holds, and in Rosenzweig-MacArthur the enrichment that takes the system from rest into a cycle.
Chooses Lotka-Volterra, a conservative cycle whose size is held where you set it, or Rosenzweig-MacArthur, which settles onto a limit cycle of its own.
An attenuverter, -1 to +1, scaling the CV into the balance.
An attenuverter, -1 to +1, scaling the CV into the boom-bust size.

inputs.text: Adds to the RATE knob at 1V per octave, setting the speed the simulation runs at.
Modulates the balance, at a tenth per volt through its attenuverter.
Modulates the boom-bust size, at a tenth per volt through its attenuverter.
A continuous force added to the prey population at half a unit per volt: a short gate perturbs the cycle, and an audio-rate signal cross-modulates it.

outputs.text: The prey population centred on its equilibrium, soft-clipped to ±5V.
The predator population centred on its equilibrium, soft-clipped to ±5V.
A 10V pulse 1ms long at each local maximum of the prey population.
A 10V pulse 1ms long at each local maximum of the predator population.

notes: Changing the mode switch re-seeds the simulation, so the cycle restarts from its default state rather than carrying over.
The peak outputs are most usable at LFO and low audio rates; at high rates the pulses crowd together.
